sources.name: SPD approved crime records
sources.notes: Daily approved offense records, report numbers and blurred blocks. Ballard North / South, burglary code 220, since Jan 2025. Business type and restaurant name are not supplied.

sources.name: SPD calls for service
sources.notes: Ballard burglary-related calls since Jan 2025, deduplicated by CAD event number rather than officer dispatch. Initial and final call types can differ. Calls are not verified crimes; commercial does not mean restaurant.

sources.name: SPD Blotter
sources.notes: Official selected case summaries. RSS is checked for Ballard restaurant/property-crime context; the blotter is not a comprehensive report listing.

sources.name: SPD recent response and crime maps
sources.notes: Official map of closed responses in the last 24 hours and approved offenses in the last seven days. Linked for independent checking; not scraped or counted again.

sources.name: SPD Crime Dashboard
sources.notes: Official citywide and neighborhood context using NIBRS terminology. All-premises burglary totals must not be presented as restaurant totals.

sources.name: Police public records requests
sources.notes: Request the actual report narrative using a report number. Open-data listings are metadata, not full police reports, charges or case outcomes. No requests have been submitted automatically.

sources.name: My Ballard
sources.notes: Current reporting plus three search-archive RSS channels for break-ins, burglary and vandalism. These are four channels from one publisher, not four independent corroborating sources.

sources.name: KING 5
sources.notes: Public local-news RSS checked for Ballard incident and food-business context. Some full articles are access-restricted; an accessible headline alone is not enough to map an incident.

sources.name: FOX 13 Seattle
sources.notes: Local reporting and owner interviews. Public RSS checked for Ballard incident and food-business context.

sources.name: KIRO 7
sources.notes: Verified public RSS endpoint, checked for Ballard incident and food-business context. Closure reporting is kept distinct from claims about why a business closed.

sources.name: The Seattle Times
sources.notes: Project inspiration and a potential reporting source. Full-text/feed access was not available during research. No paywall or access-control bypass; no automatic ingestion is claimed.

sources.name: KOMO News
sources.notes: Additional original local reporting for manual source discovery. An official working RSS endpoint was not verified, so it is not shown as connected.

sources.name: Ballard Alliance
sources.notes: Business-community updates and public-safety context. Its public RSS feed is checked. Private member reports and internal incident logs are not accessed.

sources.name: Saleh's owner Instagram post
sources.notes: Direct owner-post link supplied by My Ballard. Post text was not independently readable without platform access. Two described incidents remain two records, not additional incidents because they appear on social media.

sources.name: Sloop Tavern owner Instagram post
sources.notes: Public post link embedded in the verified news report. The reported third incident in a year is contextual history; undated earlier incidents are not invented as separate map entries. No automatic Instagram scraping.

sources.name: Dough Joy owner Instagram reel
sources.notes: Owner reel linked in My Ballard's report. No video, faces or suspect images are copied. News reporting supports the mapped entry; the reel is linked for context, not independent corroboration.

sources.name: Highland Espresso on Instagram
sources.notes: Business profile linked in original reporting. A profile is a discovery channel, not evidence for a new incident. Official platform access or owner submissions are needed for reliable ongoing ingestion.

sources.name: My Ballard on Facebook
sources.notes: Public publisher page linked from My Ballard. Links may be reviewed by a person; private groups, comments behind login and personal profiles are not scraped.

sources.name: Ballard Alliance on Facebook
sources.notes: Public business-community page linked from the Alliance website. Manual discovery only; no private member data or automated Meta access is configured.

sources.name: Visit Ballard on Instagram
sources.notes: Public community account linked by Ballard Alliance. Useful for business updates and recovery appeals, not automatically treated as an incident feed.

sources.name: r/Seattle public discussions
sources.notes: Public discussion discovery only. Automated RSS access returned HTTP 403, so no Reddit posts are ingested or claimed as monitored. Community claims require a business source or independently checked reporting.

sources.name: r/SeattleWA public discussions
sources.notes: An additional public search channel, not a connected API. No posts are ingested. Neither votes nor repeated anecdotes establish an incident, location or suspect identity.

sources.name: KING 5 Ballard video report
sources.notes: Publicly indexed broadcast report about Ballard break-ins. Manual review only. A repost of a broadcast is not an independent extra source or an additional incident.

sources.name: Highland Espresso recovery fundraiser
sources.notes: Owner-linked recovery appeal referenced by original reporting. Fundraising goals and amounts raised are not incident-loss estimates and are not added to cost totals.
